item.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
item.description: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.

item.title: French police officers convicted of racist assault
item.description: A French court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the beating of a black music producer in 2020. It also recognized the assault on Michelle Zecler was racially motivated.

item.title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
item.description: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.

item.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
item.description: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.

item.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
item.description: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.
